extracted.intended_audience: journalism educators, reporting teachers, editors and others interested in journalism education
extracted.subtask_description: Assess how basic newswriting and reporting courses are organized, taught, and assessed across U.S. colleges and universities, based on a questionnaire survey of reporting teachers. The focus is on course level, instructor background, content and structure, classroom practices, and student evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of students the course is focused at
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of students the course is focused at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The questionnaire collected data to indicate whether basic newswriting courses are targeted to particular student levels (e.g., freshman, sophomore, upper-division, graduate). Statistical data based on responses are presented in table form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the instructors assigned to these courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The background of the instructors assigned to these courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey responses describe instructor qualifications and backgrounds; this dimension helps evaluate how instructor experience and training relate to course content and effectiveness. Commentary from teachers is included in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature, structure, and content of the courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature, structure, and content of the courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what topics are taught, how the course is organized (lectures, discussions, labs), syllabus elements, and the overall scope of basic newswriting and reporting classes. Data are summarized statistically and discussed in narrative form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emphasis given to various topics in the lectures and discussion sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of emphasis given to various topics in the lectures and discussion sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey measured how much class time and emphasis instructors give to specific topics within newswriting courses; results are tabulated to show relative emphasis across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of labs and writing situations
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequency of labs and writing situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric captures how often students engage in lab work or practical writing assignments (news stories, exercises), indicating hands-on practice frequency. Survey statistics report typical lab/writing frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of student copy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to how student-written copy is handled—editing practices, submission and revision workflows, publication opportunities, and instructor feedback mechanisms. The report summarizes common practices reported by teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of student achievement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers grading methods, assessment criteria, tests, portfolios, performance evaluation, and other ways instructors measure student learning in basic newswriting courses. Survey data and teacher commentary illuminate prevailing evaluation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher comments and suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: A selection of teacher comments and suggestions for the improvement of basic newswriting courses is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report presents qualitative suggestions and recommendations from instructors about improving course content, pedagogy, and assessment; these provide practical guidance and identify perceived gaps or best practices.
